# Merged cells ending in exact-height rows

Original python-docx (MIT) controls, generated by
`tools/merged_ending_rows_fixture.py 14` and `15`. No corpus content or third-party
document engine is included. The reference application exported both 16-page references.
Each mode covers AA, AE, EA, EE, AEA, AAE, EAA and EAE row-height sequences
(A = atLeast, E = exact), with either a tall paragraph or a nested table.

The merged source ends below its declared span. The reference application grows a final flexible row;
when the final row is exact, it keeps preceding rows at their own heights and
clips merged content. The native PDF retains clipped text operators, so the
recorder checks rendered ink rather than assuming extracted text is visible.
The 144 marker regions include intentionally blank regions. Source/PDF hashes
bind the recorded expectations. All 16 mode-15 page pairs were inspected; both
modes pass native pixel-bound checks.

Relevant OOXML: Part 1 §§17.4.80 trHeight, 17.18.37 ST_HeightRule,
17.4.84 vMerge and 17.4.85 vAlign. These define heights and merges without an
explicit algorithm for allocating oversized merged content across mixed rows.
The final-row allocation/clipping rule is recorded as native measured reference
behavior, rather than a claimed normative allocation requirement.

Reproduce native PDFs using tools/export-reference.ps1, then run
`python tools/record_merged_ending_rows.py`. Unit and browser tests cover row
geometry, hidden-source caret bounds, no-edit ZIP preservation, editing,
unrelated parts, exact undo and reopening. The unit fixture tests allow 60s
for their 16-page import/export checks; this is not a rendering-time budget.
